# event trajectory

- **CURIE:** [`gmeow:eventTrajectory`](gmeow-eventTrajectory.md)
- **IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/eventTrajectory>
- **Category:** property
- **Defined by:** [`gmeow:slices/events`](../../slices/events.md)
- **Box roles:** [RBox role](../boxes/rbox.md) ([What is this?](../../four-boxes/index.md))

The trajectory of a moving event — a parade, march, migration, or procession — describing its continuous space-time path. Reuses the [`gmeow:Trajectory`](../classes/gmeow-Trajectory.md) facility from the locations module (trajectory design). Non-functional: competing trajectory claims from different sources coexist ([Principle 9](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-ontology/blob/main/CONSTITUTION.md#principle-9)).

## Usage Advice

### Use when

- Use for the continuous space-time path of a moving event — a parade, march, migration, or procession — when the route itself, not just its endpoints, must be modelled.

### Avoid when

- Avoid it when two discrete endpoints suffice (use [`gmeow:eventFromLocation`](gmeow-eventFromLocation.md) / [`eventToLocation`](gmeow-eventToLocation.md)) and avoid collapsing competing routes — keep it non-functional so standpoint-indexed trajectories coexist.

### How to use

- Point the [`gmeow:Event`](../classes/gmeow-Event.md) at a [`gmeow:Trajectory`](../classes/gmeow-Trajectory.md) from the locations module rather than minting a parallel path class; carry source-specific routes as coexisting claims.

### Examples

- ex:parade [`gmeow:eventTrajectory`](gmeow-eventTrajectory.md) ex:downtownRoute.
